subject: Q3 close: Everwell carveout - deterministic model pinning & rollout SLA request
messages:
From: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.ai>
To: Product Team <jonas.weber@redwood.ai>, Eng Infra <marcus.lin@redwood.ai>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>, Jasmine Liu <jasmine_liu@redwood.ai>, Mark Dsouza <mark.dsouza@everwellfin.com>
Date: 2027-08-10T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Q3 close: Everwell carveout - deterministic model pinning & rollout SLA request

Hi team,

Everwell is in final procurement and their security/compliance and SRE teams have a hard ask: they need "deterministic model pinning" per-tenant for a carveout pilot (no multi-tenant fallback for the Canary cohort) and an SLA for rollout behavior during bursts. Procurement wants written confirmation by EOW 8/13 that we can (a) guarantee a pinned model variant for a named tenant and (b) provide an operational fallback policy that won't break their SLAs.

Summary of asks (attached: everwell_requirements_v1.pdf):
- Per-tenant deterministic pinning to a specific model variant (model_id + quant/profile)
- Rollout SLA: max 250ms p95 latency for 90% of tokens during steady state; documented fallback to a compatible variant if we cannot maintain the pin under saturation
- Auditability: per-token trace id and deployment version stamped in logs for the tenant
- Lead time: they want this enabled for a 2-week pilot starting 9/20 (Q3 close motion)

This is a strategic mid-market close (~$1.2M ARR first year). Ben and I will push commercial if engineering can offer a low-risk path + timeline. Please advise feasibility, minimal-scope approach, and rough ETA. If we can provide a canary-style soft pin with documented fallbacks, that may be acceptable commercially.

Thanks,
Laura
Laura Bennett
Enterprise AE, Redwood Inference
---
Attachment: everwell_requirements_v1.pdf (12 pages)
Attachment: hubspot_HW-5579-summary.pdf

From: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.ai>
To: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.ai>
Cc: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.ai>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>
Date: 2027-08-10T12:45:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Q3 close: Everwell carveout - deterministic model pinning & rollout SLA request

Laura — thanks for the clear brief and the attachments. High level response from Product after an initial sync with Infra/Runtime:

What we can do (low-effort / low-risk):
- Soft pinning (config flag per-tenant): route tenant requests preferentially to a target model variant and bias scheduler for affinity. This keeps requests on the preferred path but allows automatic fallback to a compatible variant if capacity unavailable.
- Enhanced observability: add tenant tag/version to trace events and include a short audit manifest in logs (no schema-breaking changes).

What requires more work (medium effort):
- Strict deterministic pinning without any fallback requires dedicated residency or guaranteed capacity lanes for the tenant (reserved pools). That touches Dedicated/DH autoscaler and will need a capacity reservation + infra changes.
- Rollout SLA guarantees under burst load are operational commitments tied to reserved capacity and queueing guarantees.

Request to Sales/Product: which of the two options does Everwell need? If they require strict deterministic pinning we need to scope capacity reservation and an infra schedule. If soft pinning is acceptable, we can deliver a config + tracing + contractual note in ~4 weeks (dev + 2-week dogfood + SRE runbook).

I'll sync with Marcus to get an engineering estimate — tagging Marcus for detailed feasibility and rough timeline.

- Jonas
Director, Product Management

From: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.ai>
To: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.ai>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.ai>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>, Jasmine Liu <jasmine_liu@redwood.ai>
Date: 2027-08-11T15:08:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Q3 close: Everwell carveout - deterministic model pinning & rollout SLA request

Laura / Jonas — technical note from Infra/Runtime:

Feasibility options and rough estimates:
1) Soft pin (preferred minimal path) — 3-5 engineer-weeks
   - Scheduler affinity flag per-tenant; preference window to keep KV cache warm for pinned tenants; best-effort affinity without strict capacity reservation
   - Add tenant/version tags to trace logs and a lightweight manifest writer (audit)
   - Allow automatic fallback to a compatible variant (configurable policy)
   Risks: under extreme saturation pinned tenants may fall back, but policy can attempt retry/backoff and record events for audit.

2) Hard pin (strict determinism) — 8-12 engineer-weeks + infra reservation changes
   - Requires changes to autoscaler to support reserved lanes and to admission controller to enforce tenant isolation for pinned models
   - Needs dedicated GPU pool or strict capacity allocation (we can leverage Dedicated product but that impacts billing/contract)
   Risks: higher ops complexity and longer lead time; requires cross-team (Capacity Eng, Billing) planning.

Operational note: if Sales can commit to a Dedicated commitment or a short-term reserved capacity for the pilot, we can compress Hard pin to ~6-8 weeks by scheduling an infra sprint and prioritizing work.

Attachments: implementation_notes_summary.txt (high level checklist)

Recommendation: if Everwell will accept the soft-pin with clear fallback semantics + audit trail, we can ship in ~4 weeks and meet the 9/20 pilot. If not, we'll need a commitment to reserved capacity (commercial) and a larger delivery window.

I'll draft a short scoping doc with milestones once Sales confirms which path to take.

-Marcus
Staff Software Engineer, Runtime

From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>
To: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.ai>, Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.ai>, Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.ai>
Date: 2027-08-12T17:45:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Q3 close: Everwell carveout - deterministic model pinning & rollout SLA request

Team — quick commercial decision from our side after a call with Mark (Everwell):
- Everwell prefers the hard guarantee but is willing to accept the soft-pin for the pilot IF we (a) deliver the soft-pin + audit trail by 9/20, (b) document the fallback policy clearly in the SOW, and (c) commit to a decision point after the pilot where they can convert to reserved capacity with a 30-day notice.

Action items:
1) Product/Eng: confirm scope for the soft-pin delivery and produce a milestone plan (dev, internal dogfood, SRE runbook) by EOD 8/17.
2) Sales: I'll update the SOW to spell out the fallback behavior and the conversion option; I will also lock in the commercial ask for reserved capacity as an addendum in the hubspot deal.
3) Legal/Procurement: Laura — please coordinate with Mark's procurement on the conversion clause and timeline.

Ben
VP, Enterprise Sales
